result.summary:
Reworked docs/agents/design/REQ-040-schema.md per handoffs/WF02-REQ-040/step-01b-code-design-validator.json's BLOCKER (Sec1 contained a complete, copy-paste-ready Drizzle pgTable("invite_list_entries", ...) definition -- real .references() FK calls, real column-builder calls, a real named uniqueIndex() -- which is implementation code, violating DATA-DESIGNER's own role-file 'Forbidden: Writing implementation code, migrations included' clause and Step 1b check (d)).

Fix applied, formatting only, no design decision changed: removed the ```ts export const inviteListEntries = pgTable(...) code block from Sec1 in its entirety. The preceding Column|Type|Nullable|Default|FK prose table (unchanged) remains the authoritative, complete specification of every column, type, nullability, default, and FK/cascade behavior. In its place, the 'Reference shape' paragraph now names the same primitives conceptually in prose -- a uuid PK defaulting to a random value; four uuid FKs (event_id->events.id required, user_id->users.id required, invite_code_id->invite_codes.id optional/nullable, added_by->users.id required), each ON DELETE RESTRICT; a nullable opened_at timestamp; three text columns (name required, company/position optional); the created_at/updated_at timestamptz pair; and the named uq_invite_list_entries_event_user unique index on (event_id, user_id) -- with no literal .references()/.notNull()/.defaultNow()/pgTable() call syntax, matching REQ-031-schema.md/REQ-032-schema.md's precedent (neither contains a full new-table pgTable() block; REQ-032-schema.md's two ```ts fences are single-line quotes of an EXISTING column, not a novel table's complete definition).

Scanned the rest of the document for any other executable code that may have crept in. Found one: Sec4.2's relink mechanism was stated as a literal, executable two-statement SQL block (UPDATE ... SET ... WHERE ... NOT EXISTS (SELECT ...); DELETE FROM ... WHERE ...) describing the actual UPDATE-then-DELETE relink sequence BACKEND-DEV would implement. Converted this to prose: Step 1 is now described as 'a conditional repoint' (update every row pointing at A to point at B, but only where no row already exists for that same event under B), Step 2 as 'cleanup of the leftovers' (delete whatever rows step 1's condition skipped), both inside one transaction. No SQL keywords/syntax remain. Re-verified via grep for ``` code fences across the full document after the edit -- zero matches; the document is now code-fence-free throughout.

No design decision was revisited or changed: the UNIQUE(event_id, user_id) constraint (Sec2), hard-delete-not-soft-remove (Sec3), the two-step relink UPDATE/DELETE sequence's logic and atomicity (Sec4, same mechanism, prose form only), and the business-card field placement on invite_list_entries rather than profiles (Sec1.3) are all identical in substance to the version CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR already confirmed correct in step-01b -- only the Sec1 pgTable() block's removal and Sec4.2's SQL-to-prose conversion changed.
